title: Use angle relationships and exact geometric facts
chapter: Use angle relationships and exact geometric facts
goal: Worked example: the angle outside a triangle.

scenes.visual: Triangle ABC with angle A marked 48 and angle B marked 67. Side BC is extended past C to a point D. The angle ACD has a question mark.
scenes.narration: Triangle A B C has an angle of forty-eight degrees at A and sixty-seven degrees at B. The side B C is extended beyond C to a point D. Find the angle A C D, the angle outside the triangle.

scenes.visual: Inside the triangle the angle at C fills in: 180 minus 48 minus 67 gives 65.
scenes.narration: First find the angle inside the triangle at C. The three angles total one hundred and eighty. One hundred and eighty minus forty-eight minus sixty-seven is sixty-five degrees.

scenes.visual: The line B C D highlighted as straight. Inside angle 65 and outside angle share it. 180 minus 65 gives 115.
scenes.narration: B, C and D lie on a straight line. The inside angle and the outside angle at C together make one hundred and eighty. So the outside angle is one hundred and eighty minus sixty-five: one hundred and fifteen degrees.

scenes.visual: The angles 48 and 67 lift from A and B and slide into the outside angle, filling it exactly. 48 and 67 make 115.
scenes.narration: Notice that forty-eight plus sixty-seven is also one hundred and fifteen. That is no accident. The outside angle of a triangle always equals the sum of the two inside angles furthest from it.

scenes.visual: The top corner A slides sideways, changing angles A and B to 60 and 55. The outside angle stays 115.
scenes.narration: Check with a different triangle. If the far angles were sixty and fifty-five, the inside angle at C would be sixty-five again, and the outside angle one hundred and fifteen. The shortcut and the long method agree.

scenes.visual: Line: "outside angle equals the sum of the two far inside angles". Notebook prompt.
scenes.narration: The outside angle equals the sum of the two far inside angles. Rebuild this argument, then find the outside angle when the far angles are thirty-five and eighty degrees.

notebook_exercise: A triangle's two far interior angles are 35 and 80 degrees. Find the exterior angle.
